Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a compact mutual action plan (MAP) and a short network checklist that lays out what we typically need to get a POC environment running end-to-end. For the Biocare evaluation specifically we want to lock down the following items so we can meet the proposed close window:

- Org setup & admin invite (Redwood organization + RBAC)
- API key provisioning (ephemeral vs long-lived)
- IP allowlist entries (customer firewall & test CIDRs)
- VPC peering details (if you want private peering vs public allowlist)
- Service account and role requirements for telemetry (optional)
- Acceptance criteria & sample test prompts/datasets

Proposed target milestones (high level):
- May 12: Org invite + initial admin access confirmed
- May 13: API keys issued + sample integration test
- May 15: IP allowlist in place and first smoke test
- May 20: VPC peering window (if required) and full performance test
- May 28: POC acceptance / close (subject to test pass)

Can you confirm whether procurement needs anything before we issue an SOW, and whether VPC peering is required for your evaluation or if an IP allowlist is sufficient for now?

Attaching: Biocare_MAP_20260511.pdf (summary MAP), redwood-network-checklist.xlsx (network items).

If those dates look reasonable I can set a 30-minute kickoff Tuesday (May 13) with Neha and Jonas on the technical side.

- VPC peering: we support both. If you prefer peering, we'll need: VPC ID, CIDR block(s) for the peering, and a primary contact for route table updates.
- SOW: we'll prepare a brief SOW and attach to the MAP. Monica on CS can fast-track the billing flow once SOW terms are agreed.

Subject: Internal: Technical checklist and peering notes for Biocare POC

Rachel / Jonas — internal runbook notes for the kickoff and handoff. I'm drafting a short peering template we'll send to Biocare; posting the high-level points here so Rachel can forward the relevant bit:

- API keys: we can create scoped keys with the following TTLs: 30m (ephemeral), 2h (dev), 30d (integration). Recommend 2h for developer sessions and 30d for CI smoke tests.
- Service accounts: create a service account named svc-biocare-poc with role "inference.read" + telemetry if they want usage metrics.
- IP allowlist: ask for one or two /24 ranges for smoke tests; we do not recommend using single IPs for high-availability tests.
- VPC peering requirements:
  * Our side: vpc-redwood-prod (us-west-2), acceptor route propagation enabled
  * Customer: need VPC ID, ASN (if using private BGP), and route table entries for test subnets
  * Peering window: prefer a 2-hour scheduled window (09:00–11:00 PDT) to run connectivity and performance verification
- Firewall & egress: confirm whether Biocare egress will NAT to a stable IP; this matters for allowlisting on the customer side.

I'll attach the peering template and the network-checklist.xlsx (already pre-filled) and recommend we send that in the kickoff email so Alex has everything to hand.

Neha Kapoor
Staff Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
